text:
Molly (Partnerships): FYI we got another request from a hardware partner for the marketplace listing. They want SOC reports, pen-test artifacts, and an attestation signed by Redwood legal. Who owns coordinating the uploads?
Dinesh S (Security): I can own verification of the artifacts (check hashes, redaction, ensure scope matches). I won't do the actual upload to partner storage though. We need a clear owner for ingest + TTL.
Alex P (Cloud Partnerships): I can coordinate with the partner on where they expect the bundle (GCP artifact registry vs Azure blob vs S3). Preference is presigned S3 for cross-cloud simplicity. We should also decide whether to combine artifacts into one archive or keep them per-report.
Jonah L (Marketplace Eng): Can we standardize on per-report files with a small manifest (json) describing scope, assessor, date, and contact? That makes automated validation easier. Example manifest schema we can agree on: 
```
{
  "report_type": "SOC2",
  "assessor": "Acme Labs",
  "scope": "infra + control plane",
  "report_date": "2025-11-03",
  "hash": "sha256:...",
  "sensitive": false
}
```
Molly (Partnerships): +1 on manifest. Partner asked about retention — they want us to hold artifacts indefinitely for the listing. Legal says we need retention policy and redaction capability.
Dinesh S (Security): We should limit indefinite retention. Proposal: default TTL 12 months for raw artifacts, with options to extend to 36 months by request and legal approval. Sensitive artifacts (raw pen-test logs, PII) should be short TTL or require encrypted-holding with explicit owner. Also: mandate KMS-wrapped S3 uploads.
Alex P (Cloud Partnerships): For uploads, I'll generate presigned PUT URLs that expire after 1 hour. We'll ingest into a Redwood bucket with lifecycle rules. Sample presign snippet for our infra team: 
```bash
aws s3 presign s3://redwood-marketplace-evidence/partner-<id>/<file> --expires-in 3600
```
Jonah L (Marketplace Eng): After upload, we run an automated verifier. If manifest/hash mismatch -> mark as "rejected" and notify partner with a short failure reason. If accepted, we mint a signed attestation artifact that the partner can share in their listing.
Molly (Partnerships): Who can sign the attestation? Partner expects Redwood legal + security sig. Does security-bot have a workflow we can use?
Dinesh S (Security): Security will sign the attestation after manual review. Legal needs to provide a templated attestation. We should avoid custom signed statements per partner. One template with placeholders.
security-bot: Automated scan report: 1) manifest schema validation: PASS; 2) hash check: PENDING (awaiting upload); 3) malware scan: PENDING
Alex P (Cloud Partnerships): Edge case: hardware partners sometimes provide vendor-supplied third-party pen-test reports containing embedded customer data. Need a redaction step before we store. Who does redaction?
Dinesh S (Security): We'll require partners to submit redacted versions first. If they cannot, we run an allowed redaction service but that requires an NDA amendment and engagement with Compliance. That's a longer flow.
Molly (Partnerships): Timeline request from partner: "we want listing live in 3 weeks". Realistic?
Jonah L (Marketplace Eng): If partner prepares artifacts and manifests on day 0 and we provide presign same day, then automated validation + manual security review ~5 business days. Legal attestation depends on queue but usually 3-7 business days. So 3 weeks is tight but possible if partner moves fast. I'll make a small checklist we can send them.
Molly (Partnerships): Please drop that checklist here and I'll forward. Also need escalation path if artifacts fail verification.
Jonah L (Marketplace Eng): Checklist draft: 
- Partner provides manifest.json for each report
- Attach redacted copies only (or request redaction service)
- Upload via presigned PUT URLs we provide
- Include assessor contact in manifest
- Confirm retention TTL preference (12/24/36 months)
- Accept terms for Redwood to host artifacts per marketplace policy
Escalation: if verification fails, partner has 48 hours to remediate/replace file. After 48h, partnership lead gets an escalation email to Molly + Dinesh.
Dinesh S (Security): I'll add acceptance criteria for pen-test artifacts: must include scope statement, dates, hash, and a signed assessor cover. If missing those, auto-reject.
Molly (Partnerships): Perfect. Alex, can you start the presign + bucket lifecycle infra and attach the example policy? Also need to surface the KMS key owner for legal.
Alex P (Cloud Partnerships): On it. I'll draft the bucket policy and KMS ARNs. Expect PR by EOD tomorrow.
Molly (Partnerships): Thanks all — will route the partner email once Jonah posts the checklist link. :thumbsup:
